newsitem.title: USA: Deere Q1 up on strong worldwide demand.
newsitem.headline: Deere Q1 up on strong worldwide demand.

text.p: Deere & Co said Tuesday higher profits for its fiscal first quarter resulted from strong worldwide retail demand for its products, especially new tractors and combines.

Deere reported first quarter net income of $176.7 million or $0.69 a share, up from year-ago earnings of $166.2 million or $0.63. Worldwide net sales and revenues for the quarter increased to $2.4 billion from $2.3 billion.
Net sales of agricultural, industrial, and commercial and consumer equipment were $2.0 billion for the first quarter, up from $1.9 billion last year.
Export sales from the United States rose to $392 million in the first quarter from $308 million a year ago. Overseas sales also increased, rising by nine percent.
Overall, physical volume of sales to dealers -- excluding sales by the newly consolidated Mexican subsidiaries -- rose slightly from a year ago, Deere said.

The company's worldwide equipment operations, excluding financial services subsidiaries and unconsolidated affiliates, had net income of $135.4 million for the first quarter, up from $116.1 million a year ago.
Worldwide equipment operating profit increased to $237 million or 12 percent of net sales in the first quarter compared with $221 million or 11 percent of sales last year.
Worldwide agricultural equipment operating profit increased 32 percent to $195 million for the quarter compared with $148 million last year.

Worldwide industrial equipment operating profit totaled $38 million, down from $52 million a year ago, due to costs associated with continued development of new, more fuel-efficient engines and start-up expenses associated with the major engine facility in Mexico. However, sales of construction equipment products continued at strong levels in the first quarter, Deere said.

Worldwide commercial and consumer equipment operating profit totaled $4 million, down from $21.0 million a year ago, due to lower shipping activity associated with the company's asset control efforts, Deere said.
These efforts focused on providing products closer to the required customer delivery dates, enabling the company to reduce its level of asset investment, Deere said.
Overseas operating profit totaled $69 million, up 17 percent from last year.
